title: Analytica explicatio methodi maximorum et minimorum

deep.reconstruction:
Context (Problem 3 of E297): find y(x) on [0,a] making J = ∫_0^a Z dx an extremum, where Z = Z(x,y,p,q,r,...,Φ,Φ') with p = y', q = y'', r = y''', ..., and Φ(x) = ∫_0^x 𝔷 dx, Φ'(x) = ∫_0^x 𝔷' dx are running (indefinite) integrals. The integrands 𝔷 and 𝔷' depend only on x, y, p, q, r, .... The notation is dZ = L dΦ + L' dΦ' + M dx + N dy + P dp + ..., with 𝔑, 𝔓, 𝔔, ℜ (and primed versions) for the partials of 𝔷 and 𝔷'.

This page does the following.
(1) It writes δΦ = ∫ dx(𝔑δy + 𝔓δp + 𝔔δq + ℜδr + ...) and similarly δΦ'.
(2) It notes δJ = ∫ L δΦ dx + ∫ L' δΦ' dx + ∫ (Nδy + Pδp + ...) dx.
(3) It introduces V = ∫L dx and V' = ∫L' dx, normalised so that V(a) = V'(a) = 0. Integration by parts then gives ∫ L δΦ dx = [V δΦ] − ∫ V δ𝔷 dx. The bracket vanishes at x = a because V(a) = 0, and at x = 0 because δΦ(0) = 0. So the nonlocal dependence is converted into local 'effective' coefficients: (N) = N − V𝔑 − V'𝔑', (P) = P − V𝔓 − V'𝔓', and so on.
(4) It applies the repeated integration-by-parts identities for ∫P δp dx, ∫Q δq dx and ∫R δr dx. This yields δJ = ∫ δy [(N) − d(P)/dx + d²(Q)/dx² − ...] dx plus boundary terms in δy, dδy/dx, d²δy/dx², ... with coefficients (P) − d(Q)/dx + ..., (Q) − d(R)/dx + ..., (R) − ....
(5) Coroll. 1 gives the Euler–Lagrange equation (N) − d(P)/dx + d²(Q)/dx² − ... = 0. Euler remarks that this equation already 'involves the prescribed endpoint x = a' through the normalisation of V and V'. In other words, the extremal of a functional with nonlocal integrand depends on the interval.
(6) Coroll. 2 (continued on the next page) gives the natural boundary conditions at free endpoints.

In modern terms: Φ is a state variable with Φ' = 𝔷. V is its adjoint (costate) variable, with V' = L and terminal condition V(a) = 0. The page is the δ-calculus (Lagrangian) recasting of Chapter III of the 1744 Methodus inveniendi.
errors: Printed typo: the second integration-by-parts line reads '∫L'dx dΦ' where '∫L'dx δΦ'' is meant (d for δ, and the prime on Φ is omitted).
Minor: Euler silently uses δΦ(0) = 0 (Φ is taken from x = 0) to drop the lower-limit boundary term. He only states that the upper-limit term vanishes because V(a) = 0. This is correct but unstated.
No mathematical error in the resulting Euler–Lagrange equation or the boundary terms. The R-identity ∫R δr dx = R d²δy/dx² − dR dδy/dx² + d²R δy/dx² − ∫ δy d³R/dx² is correct.

ideas.what: Variation of a functional whose integrand depends on running integrals Φ = ∫_0^x 𝔷 dx. An auxiliary V = ∫L dx, vanishing at the upper endpoint, turns the nonlocal term into local modified coefficients N − V𝔑, P − V𝔓, ...
ideas.modern_name: Adjoint/costate method for integro-differential (Volterra-type) Lagrangians; equivalently, a Lagrange multiplier for the state equation Φ' = 𝔷 with transversality condition V(a) = 0
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler, Methodus inveniendi (1744), Ch. III. The costate formalism in general is attributed to Lagrange multipliers and later to Pontryagin et al. (1956–62).
ideas.where_published: Methodus inveniendi lineas curvas (E65, 1744), Ch. III; also E297 itself (Novi Comm. Petrop. 10, 1766)

ideas.what: Euler–Lagrange equation for higher-order Lagrangians, (N) − d(P)/dx + d²(Q)/dx² − ... = 0, together with natural boundary conditions from the boundary terms.
ideas.modern_name: Euler–Poisson equation and natural boundary conditions
ideas.where_published: E65; E296/E297; Institutiones calculi integralis vol. III appendix

ideas.what: Observation that the differential equation of the extremal depends on the endpoint a, through the normalisation V(a) = 0.
ideas.modern_name: Non-autonomy and interval-dependence of extremals for nonlocal functionals

deep.surprise_reason: This is a faithful δ-calculus re-derivation of material already in the 1744 Methodus, Chapter III. Euler's V functions as a costate with terminal condition, and historians of optimal control have noted Euler's handling of such integral formulas. Nothing here appears absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: Line '∫L'dxdΦ=V'∫dx(...)' matches the print, but the print itself has a typo: it should read ∫L'dx δΦ'.
In the identity for ∫Q dx δq the last term should be ∫(δy/dx) ddQ, i.e. ∫ δy d²Q/dx. The transcription is consistent with the image.
